description: India's 15-character Goods and Services Tax registration number: a 2-digit state code, the taxpayer's PAN, an entity code, a fixed Z and a check character.
India's 10-character Permanent Account Number issued by the Income Tax Department to a person or entity (AAAAA9999A).
Harmonised System of Nomenclature code classifying goods for GST and customs; 4, 6 or 8 digits.
Services Accounting Code classifying services under Indian GST; 6 digits beginning with 99.
Indian Financial System Code identifying a bank branch for NEFT/RTGS/IMPS transfers: 4 letters, a zero, 6 alphanumerics.
The 2-digit state or union-territory code that prefixes every GSTIN (01 Jammu & Kashmir … 38 Ladakh, 97 other territory, 99 centre).
The GST percentage applied to a line: one of the published slabs rather than an arbitrary percentage.
An Indian bank account number as printed on a passbook or cheque; 9–18 digits, bank-specific, no check digit.
India Post's 6-digit Postal Index Number; the first digit is a region 1–9.
Corporate Identification Number assigned by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs: 21 characters starting with L (listed) or U (unlisted).
Udyam registration number for Indian micro, small and medium enterprises, shaped UDYAM-XX-00-0000000.
A seller-assigned invoice or bill identifier; usually prefixed (INV-, BILL-) and unique per financial year.
The legal or trading name of a supplier, vendor or counterparty on a transaction.
A general-ledger account code or name from the chart of accounts that a transaction posts to.
The Income-tax Act section under which tax was deducted at source (194C, 194J, 192…).
Whether a payment has been made: paid, unpaid, partial, overdue, refunded, void.
The Indian payment rail used: UPI, NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, cheque, cash, card.
A monetary value in the transaction's currency; additive across rows.
An ISO 4217 three-letter currency code such as INR, USD or EUR.
International Bank Account Number: a country code, two check digits and a national account identifier; validated by mod-97.
SWIFT Business Identifier Code naming a bank and optionally a branch; 8 or 11 characters with a 2-letter country at positions 5–6.
A calendar date without a time component, ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD or a recognised local variant.
A timestamp with date and time, ISO 8601 or a recognised local variant, optionally with a zone offset.
Milliseconds since the Unix epoch (1970-01-01T00:00:00Z); 13 digits for current dates.
Seconds since the Unix epoch (1970-01-01T00:00:00Z); 10 digits for current dates.
A ratio expressed on a 0–100 scale.
A likelihood or share expressed on a 0–1 scale.
An email address: a local part, an @, and a domain.
A web address with an http or https scheme.
An IPv4 network address written as four dotted decimal octets.
An IPv6 network address written as colon-separated hexadecimal groups.
A telephone number in E.164 form: a leading + and up to 15 digits including the country code.
An ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code such as IN, US or GB.
The 3-digit HTTP response status code (200, 404, 500).
A log severity label: DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR, FATAL or equivalents.
The HTTP request method: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS.
An elapsed time in milliseconds.
An opaque per-request or per-trace correlation identifier attached to a log line.
The name of the service, application or component that emitted a record.
A URL path or route (/api/v1/orders) without the host.
A universally unique identifier in 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal form.
The name of a tracked product event such as page_view, signup or purchase.
An opaque identifier for the user who performed an action; identifies an individual.
An identifier grouping one user's actions within a single visit or session.
A JSON object of arbitrary key-value properties attached to an event.
The utm_source campaign parameter naming where traffic came from (google, newsletter).
The utm_medium campaign parameter naming the marketing channel (cpc, email, social).
The utm_campaign parameter naming the specific marketing campaign.
A geographic latitude in decimal degrees, −90 to 90.
A geographic longitude in decimal degrees, −180 to 180.
A city or town name.
A first-level administrative division: state, province or region.
A sub-city or sub-state locality: district, neighbourhood, borough or ward.
A postal or ZIP code in any country's format.
A free-form street address line.
An identifier for a marketplace listing such as a rental property or product offer.
An identifier for the host or seller behind a marketplace listing; identifies an individual.
The display name of a marketplace host or seller; identifies an individual.
The accommodation type of a listing: entire home, private room, shared room, hotel room.
The number of days in a period a listing is available for booking.
The minimum number of nights a listing can be booked for.
A count of reviews received.
A review rate, such as reviews per month.
The date of the most recent review.
A 0/1 indicator of whether an individual survived, from the Titanic-style sample datasets.
A ticket or travel class, typically 1, 2 or 3.
Recorded sex or gender of a person; a protected attribute.
A person's age in whole or fractional years.
The fare paid for a journey or ride.
The port or station where a passenger boarded.
A country's name in words (India, United States) rather than its ISO code.
A sales-order or transaction identifier assigned by the selling system.
A stock-keeping unit or product code identifying a sellable item.
A count of units on an order line, in stock or produced.
An identifier for a customer account; identifies an individual or organisation.
The title of a film, show, track, article or other media item.
A person credited on a media item: director, cast, author, artist.
An audience rating such as PG-13, TV-MA, U/A or 18+.
The genre or category of a media item.
The year a media item was released.
The kind of media item: movie, TV show, album, podcast.
A password, token or other secret used to authenticate; must never be exported in the clear.
A long-lived API key or bearer token issued by a service.
A JSON Web Token: three base64url segments separated by dots.
A PEM-encoded private key block (-----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY-----).
An AWS access key identifier beginning AKIA or ASIA.
A payment card primary account number, 13–19 digits passing the Luhn check.
A United States Social Security number in 3-2-4 form.
A person's birth date.
A national passport number.
A government-issued personal identity number such as Aadhaar or a national ID card number.
A hardware MAC address: six hexadecimal pairs separated by colons or hyphens.
A cryptocurrency wallet address (Bitcoin base58/bech32, Ethereum 0x-hex).
A surrogate or row identifier with no business meaning beyond uniqueness.
The title or display name of a marketplace listing.
An identifier for an employee record; identifies an individual.
An employee's job title or position.
The organisational department or unit a person or cost belongs to.
Pay: salary, wage or total compensation for a person.
Length of service in years.
The kind of real-estate property: apartment, house, plot, commercial.
The number of bedrooms in a property.
The number of bathrooms in a property.
A floor area in square feet.
The price at which a property or item sold or is listed.
An identifier for a student record; identifies an individual.
A school grade, class or year level.
The name of a course, subject or module.
A test or assessment score on a 0–100 scale.
Whether a course or task was completed: completed, in progress, dropped.
An identifier for a patient record; identifies an individual.
A clinical diagnosis code such as ICD-10 (J18.9) or SNOMED.
An identifier for a clinical visit, admission or encounter.
The number of days a patient stayed in a facility.
The monetary amount claimed or paid on an insurance or medical claim.
A population count for a geography or group.
A count of households.
A median income figure for a geography or group.
An unemployment rate as a percentage.
An age range label such as 18–24 or 65+.
An identifier for a sensor, probe or measuring device.
A temperature reading, typically °C or °F.
A relative-humidity reading on a 0–100 scale.
A pressure reading such as atmospheric pressure in hPa or bar.
The unit of measure for an adjacent quantity: kg, m, °C, kWh.
A boolean or 0/1 indicator that a transaction was flagged or confirmed as fraudulent.
A model-produced risk score for a transaction, customer or event.
The outcome of a payment authorisation or login attempt: approved, declined, error.
An identifier for a device or installation used in a transaction or session.
The last four digits of a payment card, kept for display.
The monetary amount of a banking or card transaction.
The fee charged on a transaction.
The direction of a ledger movement: debit or credit (DR/CR).
An interest rate as a percentage per period.
The principal of a loan or deposit.
An identifier for an insurance policy.
The premium paid for an insurance policy.
The maximum amount an insurance policy will pay out.
The processing state of an insurance claim: open, approved, rejected, settled.
The insurance line a policy belongs to: motor, health, life, property.
An identifier for a support ticket or case.
The state of a support ticket: open, pending, resolved, closed.
The priority assigned to a support ticket: low, medium, high, urgent or P1–P4.
Minutes from ticket creation to the first agent response.
A customer-satisfaction rating, usually 1–5.
An identifier for a purchase order raised on a supplier.
An identifier for a warehouse, depot or fulfilment location.
Units of an item on hand or in stock.
Days between ordering and receiving an item.
The cost of one unit of an item.
An identifier for an electricity, gas or water meter.
Energy consumed in kilowatt-hours.
Power demand in kilowatts.
The tariff, rate plan or rate code a service, meter or trip is billed under.
Minutes of service outage.
An identifier for a manufacturing or maintenance work order.
Units produced on a work order or shift.
A count of defective units.
The share of good units produced, as a percentage.
The outcome of a quality inspection: pass, fail, rework.
An identifier for a legal contract or agreement.
The kind of contract: NDA, MSA, SOW, lease, employment.
The total monetary value of a contract.
Whether a contract renews: auto-renew, renewed, expiring, terminated.
A compliance state: compliant, non-compliant, pending review.
An identifier for a donor record; identifies an individual or organisation.
The monetary amount of a donation or gift.
The name of a fundraising or marketing campaign.
The name of the fund or programme a donation is designated to.
A boolean or 0/1 indicator that a donation or payment repeats.
An identifier for a research paper such as a DOI or arXiv id.
The title of a research paper.
The year a paper was published.
A count of citations a paper has received.
The journal, conference or venue a paper appeared in.
The name of a government agency or department.
The name of a government scheme or programme.
The state of an application or case: submitted, under review, approved, rejected.
Days taken to process an application or case.
The monetary benefit or grant amount paid under a programme.
An identifier for a farm or holding.
The crop grown: wheat, rice, maize, cotton.
Crop yield as a quantity harvested.
Land area in acres or hectares.
The prevailing market or mandi price of a commodity.
An identifier for a sports match or fixture.
The name of a sports team.
Points or goals scored by a team.
The number of spectators at an event.
The result of a match from one side's view: W, L, D.
A Net Promoter Score response, 0–10 per respondent or −100 to 100 aggregated.
Minutes from ticket creation to resolution.
A topic or category label assigned to a ticket, document or conversation.
A person's name; identifies an individual.
Recorded race or ethnicity; a protected attribute.
Recorded marital status; a protected attribute.
A named medical condition, diagnosis or illness.
A code for a hospital, ward, clinic or facility.
A severity grading for a condition: mild, moderate, severe or a numeric level.
A coded location zone such as a taxi zone, pickup zone or delivery zone.
The generic payment instrument used: card, cash, wallet, bank transfer.
The highest education level attained: high school, bachelor's, master's, doctorate.
Hours worked in a period.
A distance travelled or between points, in km or miles.
A four-digit calendar year used as a period label.
The date an employee joined.
The date an employee left.
An employee's status: active, on leave, terminated, contractor.
The recorded reason an employee left.
The name of an employee's manager; identifies an individual.
The employee identifier of a person's manager.
Where a hire came from: referral, job board, agency, campus.
An employee performance rating or grade.
An engagement survey score for an employee.
A satisfaction survey score for an employee.
A count of special projects an employee took part in.
A count of days an employee arrived late.
A count of absences.
A development or income tier label for a country, region or household.
A rank position on an index or indicator.
The fulfilment state of an order: created, approved, shipped, delivered, cancelled.
When an order was placed.
When an order's payment was approved.
When an order was handed to the carrier.
When an order was delivered to the customer.
The delivery date promised at purchase.
The number of instalments a payment is split into.
The category a product is listed under.
A product's weight, typically grams or kilograms.
A product's length dimension.
A product's height dimension.
A product's width dimension.
How a patient was admitted: emergency, urgent, elective.
A count of visitors to a patient or venue.
Whether a person or claim is insured and by what kind of cover.
The number of passengers on a trip.
Free capacity of a facility at a point in time: rooms, beds or staff available.
The sector of an individual's employer: private, self-employed, federal, state or local government, unpaid.
A statistical weight a survey assigns to a record so the sample represents the population.
A person's relationship to the head of household in a census or survey record; a protected attribute.
An income bracket label such as <=50K or >50K rather than an amount.
An identifier for the vendor, supplier or service provider behind a record.
A two-valued indicator recorded as Y/N, yes/no, true/false, or numeric 0/1 under a flag-style header.
How often an employee travels for work: none, rarely, frequently, or an encoded level.
An employee's seniority level, grade or band within the organisation.
